newsitem.title: ESTONIA: HOIU TO FOCUS ON RUSSIA, UKRAINE.
newsitem.headline: HOIU TO FOCUS ON RUSSIA, UKRAINE.

text.p: Estonia's second largest bank Hoiupank said on Thursday it will not go to the Lithuanian market but will focus on entering Russia and Ukraine.

"We have analysed the Lithuanian market very carefully but at the present moment we have not found an investment object where a potential profit would have been sufficient," the deputy head of the PR department, Erkki Peegel, told Reuters.
"At the moment, the purchase of a bank or a financial organisation is more realistic in Ukraine or Russia," Peegel added, saying that plans for Lithuania were not ruled out in the longer term.
"Unfortunately the Lithuanian banking sector has not developed as fast in the last year as Hoiupank estimated in its analysis of a year ago," Peegel said.
Peegel added that if the bank makes a financial investment outside Estonia, it has to keep its capital adequacy at a good level. Its return on equity is over 50 percent at present.
"The investment must bring returns in a relatively short time," he said.
"At the same time, relations with Russia and Ukraine have developed quicker than expected," he said, adding that the development of those markets was the bank's priority.
Lithuania has been gradually recovering from a late 1995 bank crisis and most of the weak banks have now been closed.
The central bank recently shut another troubled bank, Taura Bankas, as it tries to maintain a tough regulatory line.
Although the Lithuanian bank market is seen as being back on its feet, popular trust to banks is low and the interbank lending market has been hampered by a mistrust between banks themselves.
Peegel said the bank is having negotiations to expand to Ukraine and Russia but it was too early to talk about results. The bank also does not want to give any time schedule, he added.
Hoiupank sees itself as a financial group and all its subsidiaries have the potential to develop outside Estonia, Peegel added.
The bank recently bought the Latvian brokerage company Invesk and its other subsidiaries have also announced plans to expand into neighbouring markets.
Eesti Kindlustus, the largest insurance company in Estonia, plans to go to St Peterburg in the autumn and Hoiupank Leasing is to enter Latvia in September.
Peegel added that Hoiupank has a very good knowledge about the Russian market from its Russian investment fund.
"Expansion into Russia and Ukraine would proceed from the clients," Peegel said.
"Estonian businesses are going to those markets actively and the bank has to follow its clients," Peegel added.
